newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait says Chevron wants to boost cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait says Chevron wants to boost cooperation.

text.p: U.S.-based Chevron Corp wants to boost cooperation with Kuwait beyond a 1994 technical assistance accord, the Kuwait News Agency reported on Thursday.
"Kuwait Oil Comapny (KOC) said today that American firm Chevron wants to develop the mutual relationship beyond technical agreements," it said.
Chevron in August 1994 began providing technical and seismic assistance to the state oil producer KOC involving about 30 Chevron scientists and engineers under a 3-1/2 year agreement.

"The company (KOC) is studying such issues, but a political decision in this respect has not been taken," it quoted KOC chairman Khaled al-Fulaij as saying. He did not give details about the envisaged development of cooperation.
Chevron chairman Ken Derr, who met Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi in a recent visit, has discussed this issue with Kuwaiti officials, he said.

Kuwaiti officials are studying whether to allow some form of direct foreign involvement in production, possibly in the form of an equity stake or a so-called super service fee, in return for help raising Kuwait's output capacity.
Mazeedi in March said Kuwait was actively considering opening up its oil industry to foreign partners but a final decision has not been taken.
"The main objective of Derr's visit...was to prove Chevron's support to KOC in aspired development of technical capacities," said Fulaij.
Fulaij brushed aside what the agency described as a rumour that KOC would not renew the Chevron technical agreement. "We, as two sides in this agreement, see it good for both sides."
But, he said the issue of renewing the agreement, which expires in 1998, has not been discussed with Derr.
Chevron officials have said they want to build a long-term partnership with Kuwait, offering the Gulf state high technology transfer in drilling, production, design and construction.
British Petroleum has a similar agreement with KOC.
